title: Protocol Temephos Bioassay
author: Lara Ferrero Gomez

steps_raw.instruction: Procedure following to analyse the sensitivity of
the mosquito larvae to the Temephos 1%
Maintenance of the larvae in the laboratory

The larvae are fed with commercial feed for fish that should be crushed and autoclaved. For larvae of the first stadiums if will add 0, 003g/larva of food and for larvae of the last stages 0, 006g/larva. To feed the 100 larvae, should use 0, 3 g and 0, 6 g, respectively. The larvae should be fed once a day and water must be renewed on an ongoing basis through periodic washes, generally every 3 days (CONSOLI& OLIVEIRA; 1994).
Dose-response bioassay 1% Temephos SG, SDS Ramcides Hop Science Pvt. Ltd.

Use 2 doses (5 to 10 kg/ha recommended by the manufacturer and 100 g/ton of water used by health agents in Cape Verde in the field) adjusted to the surface of the container. In this experiment it will use 9 transparent containers of plastic with 162 cm2 surface area containing 200 ml of water chlorine-free; 3 control containers, 3 container with Temephos at the doses recommended by the manufacturer (8 kg/ha) adjusted to the surface and 3 containers for the dose used by health agents in Cape Verde, set to the volume. For each replica will use 40 L3 stage larvae that are fed with fish food, 0, 005gr (autoclaved) to start the experience (this to prevent sway process starvation). During the bioassay will be controlling photoperiod (12:12 of light and darkness), temperature (26 ± 2° C) and relative humidity (75 ± 10%). Once applied the Temephos it will be determined the physical and chemical parameters (pH, temperature, salinity, conductivity and dissolved organic matter) using the multi-parameter (WHO, 2005). Repeated physical-chemical measurements of water will be determined after finished the bioassay. The readings of effectiveness of product will be only made 24:00 h post-treatment, determining the total number of dead larvae. The test shall be considered invalid and must repeat it if the mortality of the larvae of the negative control exceeds 20%. For mortalities above 5% will apply the corrected mortality (WHO, 2005).
